$comment: Example for ~/.claude/crew-chief-guard.json: the three levels read as lanes by how expensive a mistake is to undo. warn = reversible and contained (runs, then a reminder). confirm = reversible but wide, or costly to redo (the first attempt is stopped with a checklist, the identical retry passes). deny = hard to reverse (migrations that drop data, destroying infrastructure): this lane does not open, whatever the model says. Merge the rules you want into your own file; nothing here is on by default. Patterns match words in the command text, so adjust them to your tools.

rules.text: applies a database migration; check which database the connection string points at and that a backup exists
drops or resets a database; run it yourself, in a terminal, after checking the target
changes live infrastructure; check the workspace or kube context and read the plan first
destroys infrastructure or storage; do it yourself
moves money through a payment API; check test mode versus live and the amount
